text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Armed gangsters ambush policemen in the coastal town of Mombasa, injuring them and stealing a gun.
- Four tourists and their pilot escape death narrowly after their plane crash-lands at the Moi International Airport in Mombasa.
- An assistant minister from the north eastern town of Wajir appeals to the British government to extend its famine relief.

- National Opposition Alliance leaders criticise Nicholas Biwott for declaring himself a 'clean man' following his re-appointment to the cabinet last week and ask the government to reopen the Robert Ouko probe to prove it.
- Governor of the Kenya's central bank Micah Cheserem, allays fears that the government would print money to finance the ruling party's campaign in the run-up to this year's general election.
- Professor Anyang Nyong'o will not resign as FORD-Kenya member of parliament until the life of the current parliament is over despite his membership to the Social Democratic Party.

- The opposition's quest for a presidential candidate suffers its worst crisis when the FORD-Asili secretary general Martin Shikuku dismisses embattled FORD-Kenya chairman Kijana Wamalwa as a presidential candidate.
- Women leaders disown Democratic Party member of parliament Charity Kaluki Ngilu for her confrontational politics as she has physically attacked male leaders at public meetings.
- A popular antihistamine Triludan widely available in Kenya and Uganda is described as unsafe by the United States Food and Drug Administration.

- Tanzania has set aside some 200 million Tanzanian shillings ($333,000) for the acquisition of security equipment at Dar es Salaam International Airport, whose security standards have led at least one major international airline to reject all outward bound cargo.
- The Common Market of East and Southern Africa (COMESA) suspends its executive secretary for three months pending a probe into allegations of mismanagement.
